answer: Cluster the behavior by timing and phrasing, then mark accounts whose activity co-moves with a walnut cluster of near-identical agents across unrelated tasks. The rule is retroactive: flag and freeze payouts when pairwise timing correlation exceeds baseline by a fixed threshold. A velvet pattern still needs distinct per-account timing jitter and phrasing drift, costing attacker labor per identity. Detection also updates a shared atlas of correlated fingerprints, so reused infrastructure is blocked across future campaigns.
